items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: I'd be sitting there like two feet from Brad Gowan's feet and peewee

ctx.x: Did you all get down there? I don't remember now the policy of letting kids in under age or not. What did they do?

I don't remember. I remember when I was 13 and mostly on Sunday afternoons and they would let, they had, at that time they had a dance floor and they had three pianos lined up, three upright pianos in front of the bandstand. I remember that, yeah. And they used to let us kids sit inside the piano and actually sit on the edge of the bandstand. And I'd be sitting there like two feet from Brad Gowan's feet and peewee. And I think Chelsea Qualey was on trumpet at that time and sometimes Hackett. So that was, they…

items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: We had Nick’s in the Village where the group of players that associated with Eddie Condon played, Pee Wee Russell, Max Kaminsky, Bobby Hackett, Brad Gowans, the whole so-called Chicago style.

ctx.x: Well what a better place to learn then with your peers you know, and learn on the spot.

Well of course in those days we had 52nd Street, which was this marvelous block between 5th and 6th Avenue, which had, at any given time there was at least four or five different jazz clubs. They’d often change names and management and so forth, but it was great place to hear music. We had Nick’s in the Village where the group of players that associated with Eddie Condon played, Pee Wee Russell, Max Kaminsky, Bobby Hackett, Brad Gowans, the whole so-called Chicago style. There was a lot of live music happening

and of course the big bands were going great, all the major hotels had bands. Tommy Dorsey would be at the Astor, Benny Goodman would be at the Manhattan Room, which hotel was that — Glenn Miller, all the bands. And there was airshots, every evening there was airshots, 15 minutes from here, 15 minutes from Chicago, 15 minutes, it was just in the air you know. So there was plenty of opportunity to hear music.
